source: spec §4.6 'Proof runner (M1)' — the base/head classification table, plus plan §8 Cluster B.
invariant: `proven` requires ALL of: baseline ran and passed (or the file is new ⇒ not_applicable), head failed, expected_failure_signal appears in head output, and deps_install_ok is true. Any other combination is `inconclusive` or `disproven`. There is no other path to `proven`.
unlisted_combinations: The spec's table does not name (base=fail, head=pass). The corpus resolves it to `inconclusive`: the baseline never held, so nothing was proven, and the finding was not refuted either. What matters is that it is not `proven`.

cases.notes: The only `proven` row in the corpus. severity_inputs.proof_confidence == 1.0 and the finding becomes blocking-eligible.
We checked and we were wrong: clamp to info, blocking=false, keep the artifact, count it in the accuracy self-report.
The adversarial shape: a repro asserting the bug rather than the contract. It must never reach `proven`.

Red before the PR, red after it. Not this PR's fault, so advisory only. Note that the expected_failure_signal IS present in the head output — this row is the proof that a matching signal alone means nothing: without a green baseline there is no 'passing-to-failing' claim to make.
No manifest ⇒ no install ⇒ `import requests` raises. An install failure can never produce a `proven` finding. Not executed here because the host may happen to have requests installed.
Every other input matches the `proven` row — only deps_ok is false. This case exists to prove the deps_ok conjunct is load-bearing and not decorative.
Killed at PROOF_TIMEOUT; the finding stays advisory and the run still succeeds. Never executed here — it would cost 90 s to learn nothing.
A repo with no suite does not block proof — the repro is self-contained — but a repro that fails to collect is still inconclusive. coverage_gap is 1.0 for every finding here.

With PROOF_ALLOW_SUBPROCESS=false and no Docker daemon nothing executes at all: the artifact records skipped_no_env, the finding stays advisory, and gate.conclude(..., all_proofs_skipped_for_env=True) returns `neutral`. A missing sandbox can never turn a gate red.
